title: Gradient Release Bridge: policy-driven staged distribution with shadow mirroring
creator: Aisha Collins
description: Introduce a Gradient Release Bridge: an extensible rollout policy engine that supports fractional traffic distributions (continuous "gradient" ramps), deterministic shadow mirroring, and statistics-driven auto-rollback. This ticket covers the config schema, runtime enforcement, telemetry/metrics hooks, and a safety guard that evaluates semantic and latency regressions to gate step increases. Goals: (1) enable safe progressive exposure for model variants without manual step choreography; (2) provide a mirrored shadow path for cross-checking predictions and QA tooling; (3) surface clear rollback signals derived from both real-user metrics and evaluation prompt sets.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema v2 defined: supports graded splits (decimal weights), per-step dwell time, confidence thresholds, and semantic checks (prompt-set evaluation hooks)
Runtime enforcer enacts policy: accepts policy file, applies traffic weights to router, and prevents step increases when guard conditions fail
Shadow mirroring implemented: deterministic sampling path that sends copies to the candidate variant and stores results in a dedicated telemetry stream without impacting latency for the main path
Automatic rollback triggers: at least three pluggable trigger types implemented (statistical quality delta, p95 latency spike, and error-rate regression) with tunable thresholds
Console integration: rollout timeline and live metrics (control vs candidate) visible in Redwood Console; actions: pause, step-up, step-down, abort
End-to-end test: integration test that simulates degradations and verifies the rollback occurs and the router weight returns to safe baseline
implementation_notes: Schema: JSON policy object stored with versioned key in deployment manifests. Fields: steps[], max_ramp_rate, min_dwell_seconds, semantic_check_id, shadow_sample_rate, emergency_kill_flag
Router: implement fractional weight handler that supports sub-percent routing via reservoir sampling + deterministic hashing for user affinity
Telemetry: emit control/candidate paired events (request_id, prompt_signature, embeddings_diff_score, latency_ms, error_code) to rollout telemetry stream
Gates: Add a stats evaluator service (offline initially) that computes Bayesian credible intervals on success metrics and exposes a pass/fail API for the enforcer
Shadow mirroring: fire-and-forget writes to async queue (Kafka) and attach minimal metadata to correlate responses; do not block main request path
Rollback logic: support immediate abort, step-down by configured amount, or move-to-baseline depending on severity level
Backwards compatibility: policy engine should accept legacy canary YAML and translate to v2 where possible
Observability: dashboard with control vs candidate split, embedding drift histogram, and per-step audit log for actions taken by the engine
comments: 2025-01-15 - Design review: PMs and SRE requested a dedicated emergency_kill flag and explicit retention for shadow payloads. Action: add size cap and retention TTL.
2025-01-22 - Spike complete: measured router overhead for fractional routing ~0.6% p95 CPU on 8-core pool; shadow enqueue adds ~1.2ms tail when using sync path; changed to async queueing.
2025-01-28 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 implements schema and router hooks; awaiting review from infra/scheduling team.
2025-01-30 - Load test: simulated 10k QPS with 10% shadow sample; telemetry consumer lag remained < 30s with current Kafka config.
2025-02-02 - Decision: use Bayesian delta with 95% credible interval for quality checks; conservative default thresholds applied (0.5% quality regression or 10% p95 latency increase triggers action).
2025-02-03 - Blocker noted: deployment requires metrics tag changes from runtime to expose prompt_signature; filed ENG-25910 to add signature pipeline.
Follow-ups: create runbooks for manual rollback and playbooks for interpreting embedding-drift signals with SRE and Support teams.
